items.title: Adobe doesn't want to force AI down your throat (Deepa Subramaniam interview)
items.excerpt: Adobe VP of product marketing for creative professionals Deepa Subramaniam explains how Firefly, agentic features and multi-modal workflows are reshaping the creative pro, and how Adobe handles AI anxiety by keeping AI a choice.

items.title: The attack of the giant AI design slop monster: a survivor's guide
items.excerpt: Expanded from a City St George's HCI talk: a UX practitioner revisits last year's AI-for-UX predictions, finds research largely automated and AI design output now competitive, and lays out how designers survive the resulting flood of AI design slop.

items.title: Prototypes have always been the most effective specification - especially with AI
items.excerpt: When AI lets a PM, designer or engineer build a working prototype in an afternoon, the requirements doc moves after the build; the essay (citing UX Tools' State of Prototyping) argues the spec's new job is describing a system people have already clicked.

history_match.title: Buy vs. build is now also a UX decision, especially in enterprise

items.title: The vibe-coding revolution is coming to all the gadgets
items.excerpt: Large language models can now redesign your TV interface and upgrade your camera firmware for you; The Verge asks whether the physical world is ready to be Claude Code-d as hobbyists vibe-code hardware UIs.

items.title: The vibe code revolution: AI hackers are rewriting what your camera can do
items.excerpt: Hobbyists are using AI-assisted vibe coding to decompile and extend camera firmware on OM System, Sony, Nikon, Panasonic, Hasselblad and Fujifilm bodies, adding features the makers never shipped.

items.title: Google's Gemini can now run Mac apps and finish desktop chores in the background
items.excerpt: Google brings Computer Use to Gemini for Mac, letting the AI operate desktop apps, local files and websites in an isolated background window with a live preview while the user keeps working.

history_match.title: Transform a quick drawing into a live app with Gemini.

items.title: Stop Making AI Agents Click Through Your Web App
items.excerpt: CopilotKit argues web apps built for human clicks waste agent tokens and that WebMCP should expose functions to agents directly, adding that product design must now account for how a customer's own agent renders your product inside chat.

items.title: Human-in-the-Loop Design: Where AI Agents Should Ask Before They Act
items.excerpt: A practical framework for agentic UX: decide where human review belongs based on an action's impact, reversibility and who bears the cost, and design confirmation points accordingly.

items.title: Give the agent the existing toast helper, don't invent a new alert div
items.excerpt: Coding agents tend to drop ad-hoc fixed 'Saved' banners into pages; the post shows feeding the agent the shared design-system toast helper and its live-region accessibility contract instead.

items.title: Product design with AI: how the Webflow MCP brings my designs to life
items.excerpt: A product designer replaces the manual Figma-to-Webflow rebuild and hand-scripted interactions with an AI agent driving the Webflow MCP server.

history_match.title: AI prototyping inside your design system: a hands-on guide for design & product teams

items.title: Siemens and AGIBOT show AI agent that designs 3D printed humanoid robot grippers from a text prompt
items.excerpt: From a text prompt, a Siemens AI agent picks a gripper type for an AGIBOT humanoid, adapts its geometry in Designcenter, simulates and validates it, and prepares it for additive manufacturing, using MCP to drive the engineering software.

items.title: Comsol Conference 2026 highlights: Simulation and AI
items.excerpt: The new Comsol release adds AI capabilities including an MCP server that connects AI agents to build models, processes and equations; a keynote split simulation AI into physical AI and agentic AI workflows.

history_match.title: Into the Omniverse: How Developers Turn Ideas Into Simulations With Frontier AI Agents

items.title: AI Now Sends Its To-Do List to Human Photo Editors (Fotello)
items.excerpt: Fstoppers tests Fotello's AI real-estate photo editing (wall color fixes, custom skies, AI edit requests) and finds working photographers already relying on it, with humans handling only the AI's leftovers.

items.title: Annecy, Ottawa, Manchester programmers weigh in on GenAI
items.excerpt: Marcel Jean, Chris Robinson and Steve Henderson explain where they draw the line on AI in animation festival submissions as Manchester moves to ban genAI entries.

items.title: Forget searching for GIFs, Gemini can now make its own
items.excerpt: Gemini now turns text prompts, photos and videos into short looping GIFs using Google's Omni 1.2 Flash model, rolling out to AI subscribers globally and free in eight countries including South Korea.

history_match.title: ChatGPT will now make you animated GIFs

items.title: This artist-made Photoshop alternative has no AI and no subscription
items.excerpt: An artist built NIVA, a Photoshop alternative with no generative AI and no subscription, a pointed response from creatives pushing back against AI-first editing tools.
